pos.personaBrief: Possession-oriented side (Ballverliebt, StatsBomb 61% in the final) that used the ball as a defensive tool and denied it to opponents; Van Gaal said Milan play as Ajax play, wanting to win the game.

pro.personaBrief: Systematised build-up from keeper through Reiziger and the 6, with fast switches of play and long balls to Kanu and Litmanen; patient, but with a vertical intent and reset after slowed counters.

est.personaBrief: Van Gaal's system was everything: every position had strict tasks, players stuck to their positions, wingers stayed wide and the team spread in a 3-3-4 (Ballverliebt, Spielverlagerung).

lar.personaBrief: Wide wingers Overmars and Finidi were essential, with fast switches to the flanks and full-backs forbidden from crossing; two wide forwards in a 3-3-4.

blo.personaBrief: Hounded opponents collectively, pressed immediately after losing the ball and pressured high (Blind, La Grinta, FFT), with a high line and no deep block.

mar.personaBrief: Man-to-man by the outer centre-backs with Blind as libero, midfielders following their direct opponents (La Grinta, Ballverliebt), so individual marking is the base.

pla.personaBrief: Van Gaal imposed his own model on Ajax (stated view of changing the team to play his football), with only tweaks for opponents such as the 3-1-4-2 vs Bayern and half-time changes in the final.

res.personaBrief: An attacking 3-3-4 that went for more even when winning, played to win away from home, and valued playing football his way; entertainment and results were not in tension.

sis.personaBrief: The system was everything and the individual had to subordinate himself; even Litmanen was valued for his defensive work, and positions came before players.

jog.personaBrief: Technical, creative players (Jeder Ajax-Spieler ist kreativ) with athleticism and pressing fitness; Rijkaard a passing six, Litmanen a hard-working 10.

bas.personaBrief: Built on academy graduates (6 of the starting XI) and young players like Seedorf, Davids and Kluivert, with Rijkaard, Blind and Litmanen as senior leaders; youth were key figures from early on.

lid.personaBrief: From day one there was discipline (Blind), and the coach was the boss with the system above the individual, though he let players debate at half-time.
